rationale: The child text supplies only a generic authority formula and a temporary effective-date clause. C07 and C11 are the closest because they likewise combine an effective date with a defined period of operation, while C02 also specifies an effective date. Those similarities are routine administrative timing language, however, and there is no distinctive shared wording, parallel operative sequence, or matching substantive machinery showing that any candidate materially supplied the child's drafting template.

shared_material.child_excerpt: This order shall take effect on October 1, 1949, and shall case to be effective on January 31, 1950.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: This order shall be effective as of July 1, 1948, and the said [DIRECTIVE_REFERENCE] as amended by this order shall continue in effect during the fiscal year ending June 30, 1949, unless sooner modified or revoked.
shared_material.explanation: C07 has the strongest timing parallel, but an effective date coupled with an expiration period is routine and not independently material template evidence.

shared_material.child_excerpt: This order shall take effect on October 1, 1949
shared_material.parent_excerpt: This order shall become effective on June 1, 1949, and the said [DIRECTIVE_REFERENCE] ... shall continue in effect during the fiscal year ending June 30, 1950, unless sooner modified or revoked.
shared_material.explanation: C11 uses similar effective-duration machinery, but no distinctive language or substantive provisions connect the directives.

shared_material.child_excerpt: This order shall take effect on October 1, 1949
shared_material.parent_excerpt: This order shall become effective on July 1, 1949.
shared_material.explanation: C02 shares only a conventional effective-date sentence.
